A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable. Retained material can be matched across layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, and MultiNLI, including neural-collapse measurements, margin correlations, and controlled group-balancing analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Swin-Tiny experiments on Waterbirds and CelebA in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The retraining procedures and memory-efficient Hutchinson estimator in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Swin-Tiny is an additional evaluation architecture, not a modification of the proposed estimation or retraining procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four benchmark tasks and group definitions. The Swin-Tiny experiments reuse Waterbirds and CelebA without introducing new datasets, populations, or input-environment scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain ERM, LLR and DFR balancing variants, and the maximum-margin SVM reference. Appendix A.4 repeats these comparisons with Swin-Tiny. Classifier Retraining on Independent Splits is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a Swin-Tiny evaluation configuration, described as having a parameter count similar to ResNet-50. Existing data splits, metrics, group-ratio controls, and listed training hyperparameters remain unchanged; this extends model configurations without redesigning the original protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a substantial test of whether the findings generalize from convolutional to Transformer vision models. It repeats neural-collapse diagnostics, margin analyses, group-ratio sweeps, and class/group-balancing comparisons with Swin-Tiny, while retaining the original analyses.

E5.justification: Means and standard deviations over three experimental seeds remain the reporting convention, including for Swin-Tiny. Original Hutchinson probe counts are unchanged. Appendix C adds theoretical variance analysis but does not change the estimator, run counts, or empirical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive Swin-Tiny results in Tables 5–6 and Figures 12–19. For example, Table 6 reports margin–accuracy correlations of 0.160–0.234 on Waterbirds and 0.296–0.468 on CelebA; Figure 14 reports WGA correlations of 0.79 and 0.92. These are additional architecture-specific results, not same-setting improvements. Original numerical tables and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix C supplies Proposition 1 and a Gaussian-moment proof of the estimator variance, followed by a relative-variance derivation and an O(1/(KN)) scaling argument under a spectral assumption. v1 contains only an informal discussion of estimation errors and dimensional scaling.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central explanation of LLR through improved group balance. The introduction now explicitly defines better balance relative to uniform group proportions and qualifies that this need not maximize WGA, modestly narrowing the interpretation of that contribution.

C2.justification: The expanded Figure 4 caption explains declining MultiNLI WGA near uniform balance through an optimum that overrepresents majority groups. Appendix A.4 also interprets the Swin results as evidence that the findings extend across convolutional and Transformer architectures. Existing mechanism questions and broader-impact limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds Swin-Tiny's ImageNet-1K initialization but removes v1's explicit project-code availability statement and repository link. Hardware, software, preprocessing, and the original hyperparameter information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Nguyen et al.'s classifier retraining on independent splits, Liu et al.'s Swin Transformer, and Isserlis' Gaussian-moment formula. It also uses the already-cited Qiao et al. work to qualify uniform group balancing. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained, with localized revisions to the introduction, related work, and explanations. v2 adds appendix subsections, renames the broader-impact appendix from C to D, updates author/publication text and citation style, and removes the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with Swin-specific collapse, margin, balancing, and accuracy displays in eight new figures and two tables. It also adopts journal front matter and running headers, relocates existing displays, and standardizes some plot labels. Original figures remain, and dataset/training tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The Swin-Tiny replications strengthen empirical support beyond ResNet-50 on the vision tasks, and the uniform-balance qualification improves precision. Appendix C makes estimator variance explicit, although its dimension-scaling argument is not established for the low-rank covariance defined in Section 3.1. These useful but limited gains are partly offset by removal of the direct code link.
